content:
As announced earlier this year, Google Chrome has now switched to releasing a new version every two weeks.

Previously, Chrome had a major "milestone" update every four weeks, such as jumping from version 100 to version 101. Before 2021, Google used a six-week cycle.

The shift to major updates every two weeks aims to deliver "new features, performance improvements and bug fixes" more quickly. Each update contains less content, but the update frequency increases accordingly.

At the same time, Google says this "accelerated pace is a win for the web as a whole." Developers will be able to "confidently ship modern web capabilities, because of shorter deployment cycles, faster interoperability updates, and security improvements reaching users across platforms more quickly." The fact that each release is "smaller in scope" also makes it easier to "localise regressions."

On the security front, Google says that given the rise of artificial intelligence, this change will help "respond to fast-evolving threats."

For enterprise customers, Chrome offers an "Extended Stable" channel that updates every eight weeks: version 156 will be followed by version 160. Google says most enterprise users should opt for the stable version that updates every two weeks.

Chrome 153 starts rolling out today on desktop, Android and iOS. Version 154 will arrive on September 22.
